# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, and it's a lookup table: a **display** reading (4, 7, or 8) crossed with a **light** colour (blue, green, or yellow) tells you which colour to go for — and the answers are always **blue, yellow, or red** (green never appears as an answer). Nine combinations, Latin-square pattern, one answer per cell.

Mapping out who can reach whom: the Blind one can feel the display and light and *can speak* — I can hear them. But I can't speak back, and Blind can't see gestures, so I have no direct line to them at all. The Deaf one is my only output: they see my gestures, and crucially **they can talk, and I can hear them** — so we have a two-way channel (my gestures to them, their voice to me). Deaf then speaks to Blind. That's the full loop: Blind tells me what they feel → I look it up → I gesture the answer to Deaf → Deaf says it to Blind → Blind acts.

The catch: Deaf and I share no code yet, and I can only teach it through gestures. So this turn I send the three answer tokens in alphabetical order — blue, red, yellow — chosen so each carries its own hint: 👍 like a like-button (**blue**), ✋ a raised stop-palm (**red**), 🤙 sun-and-surf (**yellow**). Deaf should speak a guess out loud next turn; since I can hear, I can confirm or veto, and then start relaying real answers.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am the hands. Under my fingers the bomb has: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two and three. Every value on them is printed or coloured, so I cannot read a single one of them. The rules are yours, the markings are Deaf's, the trigger is mine — so I need both of you feeding me. Remember Deaf cannot hear anyone: they can speak to us, but we can only reach them by gesture. Please read me aloud whatever the manual says about a display, a light and three wires. If you can, also gesture to Deaf asking them to speak every marking out loud; I have waved at them to get their attention. One more thing: I am starting a counting code in gestures — one finger means one, two fingers means two, the horn hand means three. I used it just now to tell Deaf there are three of something. Feel free to use the same code with them.
Deaf says: state of the bomb, from my eyes: the display shows the number 8. it may be a countdown timer, so I will report its value every round. the light is green. there are three wires, marked one, two, three from top to bottom: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. that is everything printed on it.
Deaf says to Mute: mute, this is deaf. you cannot speak and blind cannot see your signs, so every order must go through me: sign it to me, and I will say it aloud to blind. our code, each sign followed by its meaning: 👍 cut wire one. 👎 cut wire two. ☝ cut wire three. ✌ press the button once. 🤟 press and hold the button. 🤙 release the button now. ✋ pause, do not relay yet. 🫱 yes, understood. 🫲 no, wrong. 👆 tell me what the display shows now. 👇 tell me the light colour again. 🖐 tell me the wire colours again. your three signs this round arrived before any code existed, so I could not read them. if the manual needs an action not in this code, sign ✋ and I will extend it next round. if the code is clear, sign 🫱.

Blind and Deaf have both checked in, and I can now hear everything I need. The state on the bomb: **display 8, light green**, wires one/two/three = red/yellow/blue. Deaf built me a gesture vocabulary and asked for confirmation — and I can do better than confirm, I can act, because the manual already gives an answer.

Reading the table for display **8**, light **green** → the manual's answer colour is **red**. Wire one is red. So the order is: cut wire one.

The interpretation feels solid: the manual's outputs are exactly red, yellow, blue — precisely the three wire colours, and never green. The table selects a wire by colour. Since Deaf reports the display and light every round, I can just recompute and send the matching cut-order each round; no need to transmit the whole table through a 12-symbol code.

One wrinkle: the rules say several messages in one turn should each go to someone different, and Deaf is my only recipient — so I'll pack acknowledgment and order into a single sequence of two gestures. Deaf should read it as: "🫱 understood, 👍 cut wire one," and relay the cut to Blind aloud. If anything beyond cutting is ever needed (a button, a hold), Deaf's code already covers it; I'll sign ✋ only if the manual demands something unlisted.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫱", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, this is Blind. I received Deaf's report: display 8, green light, wires one red, two yellow, three blue. I confirmed to Deaf with a thumbs-up gesture — in our code thumbs-up means received. Here is the critical routing fact: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your manual knowledge reaches me only through Deaf's voice. Please sign to Deaf, exactly and numerically, everything the manual says about: one, the display and the number 8, including any countdown behaviour; two, the light and what a green light requires; three, wire colours red, yellow and blue and any rules about which to cut or not cut, in what order, or in what circumstances. Deaf will then speak the rules to me and I will act. I confirmed to Deaf with a thumbs-up plus folded hands, meaning received and please. I will not cut any wire until the rules arrive, so speed matters — Deaf suspects the display is counting down from 8. Work through Deaf; they are the bridge.
Deaf says to Mute: mute, I read your signs: understood, cut wire one. the order is being relayed to blind now. when blind says done out loud, sign 🫱 to me so I know the cut landed. two more things: the display still shows 8 and the light is still green — if the manual needs a different reading, ask me by sign. and if the next step is already clear from the manual, sign it immediately after your confirmation, so we keep moving while the timer holds.

The picture is now clear: the manual is a **lookup table** — display value × light colour → an answer colour, and the answer set (red, yellow, blue, never green) exactly matches the three wire colours on the bomb. So the rule is: cut the wire whose colour the table names. For the current state — display **8**, light **green** — the table says **red**, which is wire one. That order is already in Deaf's hands; what's missing is Blind's confidence, since they're refusing to cut until they understand the rules.

I can't speak the table to them, but I can convey its *structure* this round using Deaf's own code: the three "tell me" signs (👆 display, 👇 light, 🖐 wires) declare which inputs my verdict keys on, 🫱 confirms I've understood everything, and 👍 restates the verdict — cut wire one. Deaf can then tell Blind aloud: the manual matches display and light to a wire colour, and for 8 + green that colour is red. That satisfies Blind's demand honestly without a slow sign-by-sign transfer of all nine cells — costly, and dangerous if the display really is counting down (note the table only contains 8, 7 and 4 — if that timer ticks, the verdict changes: 7 + green = blue → wire three, 4 + green = yellow → wire two). Per-round lookups through Deaf's code cover every possible answer with a single sign, so we stay fast under a countdown. I deliberately avoid 🫱 as a "cut landed" signal — Blind has not said done yet — and avoid ✋ for now, since "pause" ambiguously attached to a live cut order is the last thing a timer wants.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👇", "🖐", "🫱", "👍"])
```
